pages.text: "Wow, shiny berries!" Pipo crouched before a hill bush. Berries hung on every branch. "Like candy. I will try one!" His mouth watered.
He plucked one and brought it toward his mouth. Mom ran over. "Pipo, stop! You do not know what it is!" Startled, he stopped his hand.
Pipo tossed the berry onto the grass. "Ptoo!" Mom shook off his hands. "Good thing. Do not put unfamiliar things in your mouth." "It looked tasty..." His voice was sad.
Grandpa Sheep came uphill with his stick, herding sheep. "In the old days, we learned this from sheep." He pointed at the bush. Pipo and Mom looked.
The sheep sniffed before the bush, then turned and walked around it. None ate a berry. Grandpa said, "Sheep know. Those hurt your tummy if eaten." The ground around the bush remained untouched.
Grandpa taught an old game. "Like sheep! Sniff, and if you do not know, shake your head!" Tapping his stick, he sang, "Unfamiliar berries? Spit!" Pipo sang along.
Later, Pipo saw another round berry on the grass. His reaching hand stopped. He hid it behind his back. "Unfamiliar berries? Spit! I should ask Mom."
Mom examined it and shook her head. "This is not for eating either. Well done for asking without eating!" Pipo's shoulders lifted proudly. He crouched with both hands at his chest.

With one hand, Pipo blocked a lamb's path; with the other, he pointed at the bush. "One, do not touch! Two, do not put it in my mouth! Three, ask Mom!" Then he called loudly, "Unfamiliar berries? Spit!"
Mom lifted Pipo into a hug. "You waited instead of eating what you wanted, and asked Mom!" Unfamiliar things stayed out of his mouth. He grinned. "Unfamiliar berries? Spit!"
